title: The Indefinite Article
subtitle: un, uno, una, un' — and the partitive article dei, degli, delle.
objectives: Learn the four forms of the indefinite article.
Understand that Italian has no plural indefinite article; some is expressed by the partitive.
Apply the same initial-sound rules as the definite article.

sections.heading: Four forms, same rule
sections.body: The indefinite article (a, an) has four forms: un (masculine before most consonants and vowels), uno (masculine before s+consonant, z, gn, ps), una (feminine before consonants), un' (feminine before vowels). The rule is the same as for il/lo/la, but the forms are different. un libro (a book), uno studente (a student), una casa (a house), un'amica (a friend, feminine). There is no plural indefinite article in Italian. To express some books, some students, Italian uses the partitive article: dei libri, degli studenti, delle case.

sections.heading: From Collodi
sections.body: Carlo Collodi, Le avventure di Pinocchio: C'era una volta un pezzo di legno. una volta (once upon a time): feminine, singular, before a vowel. Modern Italian would use un' before a vowel, but una is used when the following word does not begin with a stressed vowel. un pezzo (a piece): masculine, before p, so un.

items.prompt: What is the masculine indefinite article before most consonants?
What is the masculine indefinite article before s+consonant?
What is the feminine indefinite article before a consonant?
What is the feminine indefinite article before a vowel?
How do you say some books in Italian?
Form: a book, a student, a house, a friend (f).
items.answer: un libro, uno studente, una casa, un'amica
